Posterior draws of a fit, shaped by trait

Source: R/fit_draws.R
fit_draws.Rd

Extracts the draws of an animal model and reshapes every parameter so that its first dimensions are the traits. Covariance matrices come out as trait by trait by draw arrays with named dimensions, ready to average, take correlations of, or compare with a simulated truth, instead of one Stan variable per element such as G[1,1].

Usage

fit_draws(fit, traits = NULL, terms = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A fit from lmm_animal, lm_phen_cov or lmm_animal_gibbs, a posterior draws object, or a named matrix of draws such as fit$draws(format = "draws_matrix"). Objects from back_transform also work.

traits

Optional trait names, one per trait. The default uses the column names of the response when the fit kept them, and trait1, trait2, ... otherwise.

terms

Optional names for the columns of X in the beta draws, in their order in the fit. The default uses the column names of X when the fit kept them, and the names the fit reports otherwise.

Value

A list of class fit_draws, with one element per quantity the fit holds: G, E, P, corrG, corrE, corrP as trait by trait by draw arrays, h2, sigma_G, sigma_E, sigma_P, uniqueness, communality, genetic_uniqueness, residual_uniqueness, s_G and, for correlation_prior = "size" or "shared_size" fits, size_loadings_G and size_loadings_E as trait by draw matrices, loadings as a trait by factor by draw array for factor fits, factor_heritability and factor_magnitude as factor by draw matrices, and beta as a trait by term by draw array. Every dimension is named, and draws are last, the same layout as lmm_animal_gibbs and back_transform. Quantities the fit does not report are derived when they follow from the others: P = G + E, corrG, corrE and corrP from the covariances, sigma_G, sigma_E and sigma_P from their diagonals, and h2 from G and P.

Details

The Gibbs sampler calls its residual covariance R; it is returned as E so that the two engines give the same names. The priors differ between the engines, so the draws themselves are not interchangeable.

loadings comes back **sign-aligned**: a column of \(\Lambda\) is identified only up to its sign, so a chain may visit both orientations, and averaging the raw draws then cancels the factor out of the posterior mean and out of any heatmap built from it. Each draw is flipped so that the trait with the largest mean absolute loading on that factor is positive, which is a property of the whole posterior rather than of one draw. Nothing else is changed: communality, uniqueness, factor_magnitude and the covariances are invariant to the sign anyway. A permutation of the columns or a genuine rotation between draws is *not* repaired, which is why those are read on G and communality instead. For the draws exactly as the sampler wrote them, use fit$draws("loadings").

See also

draws_mean, draws_quantile, animal_parameter_draws

Examples

k <- 2
vars <- sprintf("G[%d,%d]", rep(1:k, k), rep(1:k, each = k))
m <- cbind(matrix(stats::rnorm(40), 10, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, vars)),
           matrix(stats::rnorm(40), 10, 4,
                  dimnames = list(NULL, sub("G", "E", vars))))
d <- fit_draws(m, traits = c("t1", "t2"))
